name: the ⏱ toggle no longer drops the filter-result cache
why: Removes _invalidateFilterCache() from _msApplyLengthPrecision(). The toggle builds the same key as the filter typed before it, so the pre-toggle (empty) row list is replayed. Must fail on 'A: after the toggle, "." matches every millisecond Length' (8 expected, 0 rendered).

name: same mutation, seen from the isolation test
why: The isolation test flips the page-wide Case checkbox after the toggle, which changes the key, so it can never be served a replay: with only the result-cache drop removed it must still PASS. Recorded so the separation the spec claims is itself checked, not assumed.

name: the rewritten cells' cached COLUMN text is kept
why: Removes the per-cell cols[cellIndex] = undefined drop. Even on a fresh key, _cachedColText() returns the pre-toggle seconds text, so a Length column filter reads 3:12. Must fail on 'A isolation: a fresh key after the toggle matches every millisecond Length' — the one test no replay can explain.

name: the rewritten rows' cached FULL text is kept
why: Removes the full = null drop. The plain global filter reads _cachedFullText(), so a global query for a millisecond value still sees seconds text. Must fail on 'C: after the toggle, the global filter "11.666" finds A2'.

name: the column entry is cleared with null (the a861512 sentinel trap)
why: Writes null instead of undefined into cols[]. _cachedColText() treats only undefined as 'not cached', so it returns null and testRowMatch() throws on .toLowerCase() — exactly AUDIT.md §4. OBSERVED (2026-09-17), and earlier than first predicted: the throw escapes runFilter() inside _msApplyLengthPrecision(), so _msToggleLengthPrecision() never repaints the button and the spec fails on toggleMs()'s aria-pressed wait, before it reaches the isolation assertion. Still a failure of this test, for the reason named.
